title: Silage making (bunker type)
text:
Silage making (bunker type):
1. Harvesting
2. Chopping
3. Filling the bunker
4. Compacting (manual or mechanical)
5. Covering and sealing

When is the silage ready?
o at least three weeks (21 days) after preparation but as a rule of thumb, 60 to 70 days produces an optimum fermentation.

facts: The 5 main steps in bunker-type silage making are: 1. Harvesting, 2. Chopping, 3. Filling the bunker, 4. Compacting (manual or mechanical), and 5. Covering and sealing.
Compacting of silage in a bunker can be done either manually (using handheld pounders/tampers) or mechanically (using equipment such as a tractor).
Covering and sealing involves laying heavy plastic sheeting over the silage and weighting it down (e.g., using tyres) to create an airtight seal.
Silage is ready at the minimum of at least three weeks (21 days) after preparation.
As a rule of thumb, allowing 60 to 70 days produces optimum fermentation in silage.
